node.title: Assigning to Hash Values (updated)
node.author: haukex
node.doctext:
The thread "[id://1188980]" got me thinking about this one. The [doc://values] doc says:

Note that the values are not copied, which means modifying them will modify the contents of the hash.

This means that $_++ for values %hash; will modify the original hash values, and the following (based on [id://1188989|this AM post]) will assign to the values of the hash:

sub { @_[0..$#_] = qw/r s t/ }->(values %hash);

The above work because both the [doc://perlsyn#Foreach-Loops|foreach] loop variable and the elements of [doc://perlsub#DESCRIPTION|@_] are aliases to the original scalars. The slice in the second example is necessary, since @_ = ... would clobber the array and remove the aliasing, instead of assigning to its elements.

However, [doc://values] itself is not lvalue, meaning that values(%hash) = qw/a b c/; won't work. Neither will (values(%hash))[0] = 'a';.

Here's my "invention", which I present as a curiosity rather than a suggested solution. It makes use of [doc://perlsub#Lvalue-subroutines] and [doc://perlsub#Prototypes]. The parens on the left are necessary for the sub to be called in list context.

sub lvalues (\%) : lvalue { values %{$_[0]} } (lvalues %hash) = qw/i j k/; # works!

Since the order of the values returned by [doc://values] is random, this probably isn't particularly useful other than in the context of the [id://1188980|thread] I mentioned above:

(lvalues %hash) = shuffle values %hash;

Updates 1&2: However, note that repeated calls to (lvalues %hash) = values %hash; will only "randomize" the values once, and on older Perls the order won't be very "random" at all apparently not randomize at all, I would guess because the order of the returned values is not randomized between the calls to [doc://values]. Some interesting reading on the topic: [id://1167906] and [id://1171682]

Minor updates for clarification.
